mainTopic: פרוץ כעומד: is a partition valid when the gaps equal the standing parts? The גמרא tests this using a ברייתא about enclosing with animals and objects, and a תוספתא about partitions in כלאים.
overview: Earlier on the daf, רב פפא holds that פרוץ כעומד (gaps equal to the standing parts) is a valid partition, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds it is not. The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about enclosing an area with camels, saddles and cushions. That ברייתא forbids a gap as wide as an item, but the גמרא answers that it means a gap wide enough to move the item in and out, which is slightly bigger. Next the גמרא quotes a תוספתא from כלאים that lists three measures for partitions, depending on how wide the boards are. Its words 'its full width' are again explained for רב פפא as 'room to slide in and out.' The גמרא then reads the תוספתא's 'greater than' wording both ways. One clause seems to support רב פפא and the other seems to support רב הונא, and each side explains away the clause against it as mere matching style (איידי). A further challenge asks why the תוספתא lists boards narrower than three טפחים separately from boards of three. The answer is that the two cases have different reasons for being invalid: a goat leaping through, versus פרוץ כעומד. Finally, the גמרא identifies the 'less than three' rule with רבנן's limit for לבוד, and it begins examining the next clause, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from enclosing with cushions, sheaves and stalks
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists more objects that can form an enclosure for carrying. It adds the condition that the gap between items may not equal a full item's width. This seems to prove that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may enclose an area] with saddle cushions, with wheat sheaves, with boards, or with stalks, and then carry inside it. This is only allowed if there is not a camel-length gap between one camel and the next, a saddle-length gap between one saddle and the next, or a cushion-length gap between one cushion and the next!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that it began earlier as a proof. The closing condition, that the gaps must be smaller than a full item, is the part being used against רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a gap exactly as wide as a camel is not allowed, then gaps equal to the standing parts would seem to invalidate the enclosure. That matches רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who says פרוץ כעומד is forbidden. It challenges רב פפא, who permits it. The exclamation mark shows the גמרא presents this as a strong question.

keyTerms.meaning: Saddle cushions (or pack-saddles)
Sheaves of wheat
Stalks
One may carry (on שבת)
The full size of; as wide as
Saddle

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of the ברייתא. The first half, which lists camels and saddles, came just before. That is why camels and saddles appear in the condition even though only cushions, sheaves, boards and stalks are listed here.

phrases.english: with saddle cushions, with wheat sheaves,
phrases.notes: Continuing the list of things one may use to enclose an area.

phrases.english: with boards, with stalks —
one may carry within it,
provided that there will not be
between one camel and another a camel's full length,
and between one saddle and another a saddle's full length,
and between one cushion and another a cushion's full length!
phrases.notes: So a gap exactly the size of the cushion isn't allowed, which means פרוץ כעומד is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין גָּמָל לְגָמָל כִּמְלֹא גָּמָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud as a proof in the פרוץ כעומד debate.
steps.raayaObject: That פרוץ כעומד is forbidden (against רב פפא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא permitting enclosure with camels, saddles and cushions only if the gaps are less than one item's width.

steps.title: The gaps must allow items in and out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא speaks of gaps wide enough to bring the items in and out, so those gaps are slightly larger than the items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is speaking of a gap wide enough that one can bring the item in and take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. It says the ברייתא's forbidden gap is really slightly more than a full item's width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap that is 'a full camel' wide in practice means wide enough for a camel to pass in and out comfortably. That is a bit more than the camel itself, so the breach is actually larger than the standing part. The ברייתא is therefore forbidding פרוץ מרובה על העומד (gaps greater than the standing parts), and רב פפא can still permit exactly equal gaps. 'הכא נמי' (here too) signals that the same answer was used for an earlier, similar proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer as before applies
When it can go in and come out: a gap slightly wider than the item

phrases.english: Here too, it is when [the item] can go in and come out.
phrases.notes: So the gap is a bit larger than the item: more breach than standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by redefining the size of the gap.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference from this ברייתא. It does not decide the debate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a 'camel-length' gap means exactly equal. In practice it means slightly larger, enough to move the item in and out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a recurring tool in this סוגיא: reading 'full width' as slightly more than equal so that רב פפא's view survives.

steps.title: New proof: three measures for partitions, first measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source, a תוספתא in כלאים about partitions. It starts with the rule for boards narrower than three טפחים: the gaps between them must be under three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: It turns out you say there are three measures for partitions. For any [board] less than three טפחים wide, there must not be three טפחים between one and the next, so that a goat cannot leap headfirst through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a fresh attempt to settle the פרוץ כעומד debate. This step sets up the source; the key line for the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With very narrow boards, the rule is not about comparing gap to board. Any gap under three טפחים counts as closed (לבוד). The test is whether a goat could jump through, and a gap of three טפחים or more is too open.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a new proof
Three measures (sizes) of partitions
Partitions, walls
Will leap or spring
Headfirst, in one jump

steps.confusionAlert: This source comes from the laws of כלאים (separating vines from other seeds), not שבת. The גמרא uses it because it also defines what counts as a valid partition.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
It turns out that you say,
there are three measures for partitions:
any [board] that is less than three [טפחים wide],

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה,
phrases.english: there must not be three [טפחים] between one and the next,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִזְדַּקֵּר הַגְּדִי בְּבַת רֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: so that a goat cannot leap through headfirst.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת בִּמְחִיצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תוספתא in כלאים on the three measures for partitions.

steps.title: Second measure: gaps must not equal the boards
steps.stepSummary: For boards three to four טפחים wide, the gap must not equal a board's width 'so that the breach will not equal the standing part.' If the breach is greater, even the area facing the standing parts is forbidden. This seems to say directly that פרוץ כעומד is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: For any [board] three wide, or from three to four, there must not be its full width between one and the next, so that the breached part will not equal the standing part. And if the breach is greater than the standing part, even opposite the standing part it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the תוספתא and reaches the line that seems to prove פרוץ כעומד is forbidden. The גמרא's response will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כדי שלא יהא פרוץ כעומד' openly gives the reason as avoiding equal gaps. That supports רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and challenges רב פפא. The final clause adds that when the breach is greater, the whole partition fails, even in front of the boards that stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Its full width (as wide as the board)
Breached equal to standing: gaps equal to the solid parts
Breach greater than the standing parts
Opposite (facing) the standing parts

steps.whatToRemember: The תוספתא says the gap must not equal the board 'so that the breach will not equal the standing part.' At face value, this is strong support for the view that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden. Watch for how the גמרא answers on behalf of רב פפא.

phrases.english: any [board] that is three [טפחים wide],
and from three up to four,

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה כִּמְלוֹאוֹ,
phrases.english: there must not be its full width between one and the next,
so that the breached part will not equal the standing part.
phrases.notes: These are the key words: they seem to forbid פרוץ כעומד completely.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה פָּרוּץ מְרוּבֶּה עַל הָעוֹמֵד —
phrases.english: And if the breached part was greater than the standing part —
even opposite the standing part it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same תוספתא to the clause that carries the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That פרוץ כעומד is forbidden (against רב פפא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תוספתא's stated reason: 'so that the breached part will not equal the standing part.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the most direct-sounding source yet against רב פפא. How the גמרא handles it shapes the final ruling on partitions with gaps.

steps.title: The source continues with wider boards
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא gives the rule for boards four טפחים wide and up to ten אמות. The gap must not equal a board's width. If the breach equals the standing part, only the area facing the standing part is permitted. If the standing part is greater, the whole area is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any partition made of boards four טפחים wide, or from four טפחים up to ten אמות wide, must not have a gap the full width of a board between one board and the next, so that the breach will not equal the standing part. If the breach does equal the standing part, the area facing the standing part is permitted and the area facing the breach is forbidden. If the standing part is greater than the breach, even the area facing the breach is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the תוספתא it brought as a proof. This section deals with boards four טפחים wide and up to ten אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wider boards get the same basic rule as narrower ones: the gaps may not equal a board's width, so that פרוץ כעומד is avoided. Then the תוספתא sets out three outcomes. If the breach equals the standing part, only the area opposite the boards counts as separated. If the standing part is greater, the whole partition works, even opposite the gaps.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten cubits, the upper limit discussed for board width and for gaps
The area facing the standing (solid) part of the partition
The area facing the gap (breached part)
The standing part is greater than the gaps

phrases.english: Any [board] that is four [handbreadths wide],
and from four [handbreadths] up to ten cubits,

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה כִּמְלוֹאוֹ,
phrases.english: it is necessary that there not be between one and the next its full [width],
phrases.notes: The key word כִּמְלוֹאוֹ will be debated in step 8.

phrases.english: so that the breached part will not equal the standing part.
And if the breached part was equal to the standing part,
opposite the standing part, it is permitted;
opposite the breached part, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה עוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ —
phrases.english: And if the standing part was greater than the breached part,
even opposite the breached part, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא אַרְבָּעָה, וּמֵאַרְבָּעָה עַד עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same תוספתא from step 4, now for wider boards.
steps.raayaObject: Whether פרוץ כעומד invalidates a partition
steps.raayaSupportSource: תוספתא כלאים, the clause on boards from four טפחים to ten אמות

steps.title: Gaps over ten אמות and the doorway-frame fix
steps.stepSummary: A gap of more than ten אמות makes the partition forbidden. If stakes were set up with a braid running across their tops, forming a doorway frame, even gaps wider than ten אמות are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the partition was breached by more than ten אמות, it is forbidden. If there were pronged stakes there and one made a braid of straw over them on top, it is permitted even when the gap is more than ten אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the quote of the תוספתא. It adds a rule about very large gaps and how a doorway frame fixes them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any single gap wider than ten אמות ruins the whole partition, no matter how much is standing. But stakes with a braid across the top count as a צורת הפתח, a halachic doorway. A doorway is not considered a breach, so even a wide gap becomes acceptable. This part is not the proof itself. It just completes the quoted source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was breached (a gap opened in the partition)
Pronged or pointed stakes stuck in the ground
A braid (of straw or reeds) laid across the top
The form of a doorway: two posts with a crosspiece on top, which counts as a valid partition

phrases.english: If it was breached by more than ten [cubits], it is forbidden.
If there were pronged stakes there
and one makes a braid for them on top,
phrases.notes: This creates a צורת הפתח (doorway frame).

phrases.english: even [with a gap of] more than ten, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the תוספתא begun in steps 3 to 5.
steps.raayaObject: Whether פרוץ כעומד invalidates a partition
steps.raayaSupportSource: תוספתא כלאים, closing clause about gaps over ten אמות

steps.title: The first clause refutes רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the first clause of the תוספתא (boards three to four טפחים wide). It requires that the gap not equal a board's width. That is presented as a refutation of רב פפא, who permits פרוץ כעומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At any rate, the first clause teaches: boards from three to four טפחים are fine, provided there is not a gap the full width of a board between one and the next. This is a refutation of רב פפא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the תוספתא it quoted. It says the first clause clearly refutes רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that a partition whose gaps exactly equal its standing parts is valid. The first clause demands that the gap be less than a full board's width, which means an exactly equal gap would be forbidden. That seems to directly contradict רב פפא, so it is called a תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate: focus on this point, whatever else the source says
The first clause of a source
A refutation: a strong challenge from an authoritative source
The אמורא who holds that פרוץ כעומד is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the word מִיהַת. The גמרא deliberately builds its proof on the first clause (three to four טפחים) and sets the rest of the תוספתא aside. Do not get distracted by the later clauses; the attack rests on the רישא alone.

phrases.english: At any rate, the first clause teaches:
from three to four [handbreadths],

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה כִּמְלוֹאוֹ,
phrases.english: provided that there is not between one and the next its full [width],
This is a refutation of רב פפא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the quoted תוספתא into a direct attack on רב פפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's view that פרוץ כעומד is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא requires the gap to be less than a full board's width. So a gap exactly equal to the board is forbidden, which contradicts רב פפא.

steps.title: רב פפא explains 'full width' as room to slide in and out
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that 'its full width' means a gap the board can easily slide in and out of. That gap is slightly wider than the board. So the תוספתא forbids only a gap slightly larger than the standing part, not an exactly equal one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא could say to you: What does 'its full width' mean? A gap through which the board can go in and come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by reinterpreting the key word מלואו. It is the same answer it gave to the earlier ברייתא in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack assumed that מלואו means a gap exactly equal to the board. רב פפא reads it as a gap with enough room to move the board in and out, which must be a bit wider than the board. Then the תוספתא only forbids a breach greater than the standing part. An exactly equal breach remains permitted, and רב פפא survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Its full width: here read as slightly more than the board's width
Goes in and comes out: enough room to slide the board through easily
He could say to you: introduces a possible defense on someone's behalf

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources brought against רב פפא (the ברייתא in step 1 and the תוספתא here) are answered the same way. מלואו means 'room to slide in and out,' which is slightly more than the board. So neither source proves that an exactly equal breach (פרוץ כעומד) is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a single word's definition can neutralize a whole proof. רב פפא's position stays defensible as long as מלואו can mean 'slightly larger.'

phrases.english: רב פפא could say to you:
What is 'its full width'?
[A gap through which it] goes in and comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי מְלוֹאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא of step 7, reusing the reasoning from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a key term in the source (מלואו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מלואו means a gap exactly equal to the board, so פרוץ כעומד is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: מלואו means a gap slightly wider than the board, so only a breach greater than the standing part is forbidden. An exactly equal breach may still be permitted.

steps.title: An inference from the wording supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if the breach is GREATER than the standing part, even the area facing the standing part is forbidden. This implies that if they are EQUAL, it is permitted, which supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, because the ברייתא teaches: 'If the breached part was greater than the standing part, even the area opposite the standing part is forbidden.' That implies that if the breach equals the standing part, it is permitted. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב פפא by reading carefully what the ברייתא did NOT say. It only forbids a breach that is greater, so an equal breach must be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have said 'if the breach is equal or greater.' It only mentioned 'greater.' That silence suggests an equal breach (פרוץ כעומד) still counts as a valid partition, which is exactly רב פפא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it stands to reason (introduces support for the view just defended)
The open gaps add up to more than the standing parts
Which implies (introduces an inference from what the text did not say)
Learn from it (the proof works)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not something the ברייתא says outright. It comes from what the ברייתא left out. It is an inference from the wording.

phrases.english: So too it stands to reason
from the fact that it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה פָּרוּץ מְרוּבֶּה עַל הָעוֹמֵד
phrases.english: If the breached part was greater than the standing part
phrases.notes: The case is a partition between a vineyard and other crops (כלאים).

phrases.english: even the area opposite the standing part is forbidden.
This implies that if it equals the standing part, it is permitted.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב פפא in Step 8, the גמרא now adds positive support for him from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's view that פרוץ כעומד is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the ברייתא's clause 'פרוץ מרובה על העומד אסור': only 'greater' is forbidden, so 'equal' is permitted.

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the inference just made disproves רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who holds that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא the son of רב יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא seems to permit an equal breach, the גמרא asks whether the opposing view, held by רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, is now disproved. This sets up his defense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע forbids פרוץ כעומד. If the ברייתא really permits it, his view would be contradicted by a tannaitic source. That is a serious attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (proposes a conclusion that will be tested)
A refutation from a tannaitic source
The אמורא who holds that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support for רב פפא into an attack on the opposing view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's view that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's first clause implies an equal breach is permitted, which contradicts his ruling.

steps.title: The second clause gives the opposite inference
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the ברייתא's later clause says that if the standing part is GREATER, it is permitted. This implies that if they are EQUAL, it is forbidden, which supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say to you: By your reasoning, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'If the standing part was greater than the breach, even the area opposite the breach is permitted.' That implies that if the standing part only equals the breach, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pushes back by using the same reading method on the next clause. That reading gives the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause permits only when the standing part is greater, so an equal case would be forbidden. If we read the first clause precisely, we must also read the second clause precisely. Then the two inferences cancel each other out, and the proof is not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (gives a possible answer on someone's behalf)
And by your own reasoning (turns the opponent's method back on him)
Look at the later clause
The standing parts add up to more than the gaps

phrases.english: He can say to you:
And by your reasoning, look at the later clause:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה עוֹמֵד מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפָּרוּץ,
phrases.english: If the standing part was greater than the breached part,
even the area opposite the breach is permitted.
This implies that if it only equals the breach, it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claimed refutation by finding an opposite inference in the same ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא decisively refutes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading the first clause's wording precisely ignores that the later clause, read the same way, implies the opposite.

steps.title: Each view has one clause against it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the standoff. The later clause is difficult for רב פפא, and the first clause is difficult for רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later clause is difficult for רב פפא, and the first clause is difficult for רב הונא the son of רב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem plainly: the ברייתא seems to contradict itself, and each side has one clause that works against it. This sets up the resolution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause implies 'equal is permitted,' which fits רב פפא. The later clause implies 'equal is forbidden,' which fits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. One of these inferences must be explained away.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching
It is difficult (poses a problem)

phrases.english: The later clause is difficult for Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא קַשְׁיָא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: the first clause is difficult for Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא לְרַב פָּפָּא, רֵישָׁא קַשְׁיָא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the result of Steps 9 and 11: two clauses with opposite inferences.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both views: רב פפא from the סיפא, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע from the רישא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two clauses of the ברייתא imply opposite rulings for an equal breach, so each view is contradicted by one clause.

steps.title: The later clause just copies the first clause's style
steps.stepSummary: The later clause is no problem for רב פפא. It says 'standing part greater than breach' only to match the wording of the first clause, 'breach greater than standing part.' It is not meant to exclude the equal case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later clause is not difficult for רב פפא. Since the first clause said 'breach greater than standing part,' the later clause said, to match it, 'standing part greater than breach.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by saying that the wording of the later clause is not precise. It was phrased that way only to mirror the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause is the precise one and teaches that an equal breach is permitted. The later clause's phrase 'greater' is just matching style, so no inference should be drawn from it. Only the first clause carries a real inference, and it supports רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it taught (this wording, it also taught the matching wording); signals parallel phrasing that should not be read precisely
It is not difficult

steps.whatToRemember: On רב פפא's reading, the first clause is precise, so an equal breach is permitted. The later clause's wording only mirrors the first clause's style. The next step gives רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע the same kind of answer, so the תוספתא does not end up proving רב פפא right.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'אַיְּידֵי' answer is a common tool throughout ש״ס. It is used when one clause's wording is just a stylistic echo of a neighboring clause and should not be read precisely.

phrases.english: The later clause is not difficult for Rav Pappa:
since the first clause taught
'the breached part is greater than the standing part,'
the later clause taught
'the standing part is greater than the breached part' (to match it).

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא לְרַב פָּפָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the half of Step 12's difficulty that was aimed at רב פפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (אַיְּידֵי): the later clause's wording is not precise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause's word 'greater' was taken precisely, implying an equal breach is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'greater' in the later clause only mirrors the first clause. Only the first clause is precise, so an equal breach is permitted, as רב פפא holds.

steps.title: The first clause is no problem for רב הונא either
steps.stepSummary: Just as רב פפא explained away the later clause, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains away the first clause. It says 'breach greater than standing' only to match the later clause's wording, 'standing greater than breach.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is not a difficulty for רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. Since the ברייתא wanted to teach in the later clause 'the standing part is greater than the breach,' it taught in the first clause 'the breach is greater than the standing part.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע the same kind of answer that רב פפא just used. The wording of the first clause is just a stylistic match and should not be used for an inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 we inferred from the first clause that equal is permitted. Now רב הונא says the first clause really means 'breach greater than or equal to standing.' It was phrased 'greater' only to mirror the later clause. Now both inferences are cancelled, and the wording of the תוספתא's clauses proves nothing for either side.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it wanted to teach. Introduces wording chosen only to match a parallel clause.
The first clause of a source
The later clause of a source
The standing part is greater than the breached part

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides used the same move ('it was said only to match the other clause'). So the inference from the 'greater than' wording is a draw. It proves neither רב פפא nor רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: The first clause is not difficult for Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
since it wanted to teach in the later clause
'the standing part is greater than the breach,'
it taught in the first clause
'the breach is greater than the standing part.'
phrases.notes: It really means 'greater or equal'; 'greater' is just said to match the wording of the parallel phrase.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 13. רב פפא neutralized the סיפא, and now רב הונא neutralizes the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (איידי). The wording is not precise, so no inference can be drawn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא's word 'greater' implies that equal is permitted, against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא used 'greater' only to match the סיפא. Equal can still be forbidden.

steps.title: Why does the boards ברייתא teach two separate clauses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new challenge from the structure of the same תוספתא. It teaches boards less than three טפחים wide and boards exactly three טפחים wide in separate clauses. This fits רב פפא, but according to רב הונא both cases follow the same rule, so they should have been combined.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to רב פפא: that is why the ברייתא did not combine them and teach them together. But according to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, it should have combined them and taught them together: 'Any wall made of boards less than three טפחים wide, or exactly three, needs that there not be three טפחים between one board and the next!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. This time it uses the structure of the same תוספתא: why are its first two measures listed separately? First it says the structure fits רב פפא, and then it shows the difficulty for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, equal is fine. So with boards three wide, a gap of exactly three is allowed. With narrower boards, a gap of three is not allowed. The rules differ, so two clauses make sense. According to רב הונא, equal is forbidden. So boards three wide also need a gap of less than three, which is exactly the same rule as narrow boards. Why not write one combined clause?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view). Sets up a contrast with 'but for the other view.'
But. Introduces the side that has the difficulty.
It should have combined them and taught them together
Less than three טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: This is the SAME תוספתא from steps 3–6, not a new source. The two cases being compared are its first measure (boards less than three, step 3) and its second measure (boards of three, step 4). This time the question is not about wording like 'greater.' It is about why these two cases are listed separately when, for רב הונא, they share the same practical rule.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא עָרֵיב לְהוּ וְתָנֵי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: for that reason it did not combine them and teach them together.
phrases.notes: For רב פפא the two cases really have different rules about a gap of exactly three.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ —
phrases.english: But according to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua —
let it combine them and teach them together:
any [board] that is less than three, or three —

phrases.aramaic: צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה!
phrases.english: it is necessary that there not be three [טפחים] between one and the next!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב פָּפָּא מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא עָרֵיב לְהוּ וְתָנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the inference from the wording of the תוספתא ended in a draw, the גמרא opens a new challenge from the structure of the same תוספתא (its first two measures).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who holds that פרוץ כעומד is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If equal is forbidden, boards of three and boards of less than three share one practical rule (the gap must be less than three). A ברייתא would normally combine them, so listing them separately suggests they differ, as רב פפא holds.

steps.title: The two clauses have different reasons for being invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא kept the clauses separate because the reason for the rule differs. With narrow boards, the problem is that a young goat could leap through a gap of three. With boards of three, the problem is פרוץ כעומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the disqualification of the first clause is not like the disqualification of the later clause. The disqualification of the first clause is so that a young goat cannot leap through in one jump. The disqualification of the later clause is so that the breach should not equal the standing part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. Even though the practical rule is the same, the reasons are different, so the ברייתא taught them separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With boards less than three טפחים, a three-טפח gap is a real opening that a kid goat can jump through. With boards of exactly three, the gap of three is bad because it makes the gaps equal to the standing parts (פרוץ כעומד). A ברייתא may list cases separately when their reasons differ, so the separation proves nothing for רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualification. The reason a wall is invalid.
Leap or jump through
A young goat (kid). The standard measure for an opening that is too big.
The breached part equals the standing part

steps.whatToRemember: Same practical result, different reasons. The תוספתא splits the cases by REASON, so its structure fits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע too. The dispute between רב פפא and רב הונא remains undecided by this תוספתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common גמרא principle: a ברייתא may separate two cases with the same practical outcome because their underlying reasons differ. So separate clauses do not always mean different laws.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא דָּמֵי פְּסוּלָא דְרֵישָׁא לִפְסוּלָא דְסֵיפָא.
phrases.english: Because the disqualification of the first clause is not like the disqualification of the later clause.
The disqualification of the first clause —

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִזְדַּקֵּר הַגְּדִי בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: is so that a young goat will not leap through in one jump,
phrases.notes: This applies to boards narrower than three טפחים.

phrases.english: the disqualification of the later clause —
is so that the breach will not equal the standing part.
phrases.notes: This applies to boards of exactly three טפחים, according to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא דָּמֵי פְּסוּלָא דְרֵישָׁא לִפְסוּלָא דְסֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 on behalf of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction of reasons. The cases have the same practical rule but different underlying reasons, which justifies separate clauses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate clauses mean different practical rules, which supports רב פפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clauses are separate because their reasons differ (goat-leap versus פרוץ כעומד). Their practical rule can still be identical, as רב הונא holds.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the 'less than three' rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the ברייתא's rule about a gap of less than three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule about 'less than three': whose opinion is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a short identifying question: which תנא holds the 'less than three' rule from the ברייתא? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a gap smaller than three טפחים as fine, as if it were closed. The size limit for this rule is the subject of a known מחלוקת, so the גמרא wants to know whose side the ברייתא is on.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three (טפחים)
Whose (opinion) is it?

phrases.english: Less than three, whose opinion is it?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא's ruling that a gap of less than three טפחים does not ruin the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא of boards was used in steps 15-16, the גמרא briefly asks which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the cut-off for a harmless gap is 'less than three'?

steps.title: It follows the Rabbis' view of לבוד
steps.stepSummary: The rule follows רבנן, who apply לבוד to gaps under three טפחים but not to a gap of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the opinion of the Rabbis, who say: for less than three we say לבוד; for three we do not say לבוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבנן. They hold that a gap smaller than three טפחים counts as closed (לבוד), but a gap of three does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לבוד means two pieces close enough together are treated as joined. רבנן set the limit at under three טפחים. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, by contrast, extends it to under four. Since the ברייתא uses 'less than three' as the cut-off, it must follow רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the majority view)
'Joined': a gap small enough is treated as if closed
We say, meaning we apply the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think לבוד applies to a gap of exactly three. According to רבנן it must be LESS than three. A gap of exactly three is already too big.
steps.whyThisMatters: This identifies the ברייתא with רבנן's three-טפחים limit for לבוד. That limit is the basis for the later clauses about boards three wide and boards three to four wide.

phrases.english: It is the Rabbis, who say:
For less than three, we say 'lavud' (considered joined),
For three, we do not say 'lavud.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבנן, who limit לבוד to gaps of less than three טפחים.

steps.title: Quoting the later clause about boards three to four wide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the later clause of the ברייתא, about boards three wide and boards from three to four wide, to set up its next move.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the later clause: any (partition of boards) that are three wide, and from three to four wide...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the next part of the ברייתא, about boards that are three טפחים wide and boards between three and four wide. This is a setup line. The real point of quoting it comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אימא סיפא' tells us the גמרא is turning to the later clause of the same ברייתא in order to work through it. Having just tied the ברייתא to רבנן's three-טפחים limit, the גמרא now looks at the cases of three and of three to four. Those are exactly the sizes where לבוד no longer helps according to רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the later clause
From three up to four (טפחים)
Any that is (of this size)

phrases.english: Say the latter clause: any (partition of boards) that is three,
and from three until four —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֹשָׁה, וּמִשְּׁלֹשָׁה וְעַד אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having established that the ברייתא follows רבנן, the גמרא turns to the later clause of the same ברייתא to examine it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The later clause of the ברייתא about boards three wide and boards three to four wide (the full challenge continues on the next amud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the גמרא quotes the later clause so it can test it against the understanding just reached. The actual difficulty is stated in the continuation.
